_note: Measured results for the project. The metrics page renders from this file. Values are stored as the strings to display; do not round or recompute them.

model.name: R4
model.summary: A detector for ten dashboard warning lights, scored on 49 real, un-augmented photos it never saw in training. This page shows how well it performs and what changed between the first model and this one.
model.evaluation: 49 real, un-augmented dashboard photos never used in training (18 validation, 31 test), 145 labelled lights.

threshold_free.title: Threshold-free
threshold_free.subtitle: Ultralytics validation, macro over classes
threshold_free.note: Here precision and recall are taken at each set's own best-F1 threshold, which is why they swing between sets. The confidence-0.40 table is the fair comparison.

object_level.note: R4 fixed 15 lights R2 missed and lost 9 it had.

journey.done: Public Roboflow model for this dataset
journey.lesson: Measured mostly on synthetic icon sheets, so not comparable with real photos.

journey.result: Its own validation: 99.0% / 95.6%. Original 13 real test photos: precision 64.1%, recall 49.4%, mAP@50 0.575
journey.lesson: Validation was about 80% synthetic; the real-photo score exposed the gap.

journey.done: YOLO11s at 960 px; validation and test rebuilt from real photos only; no horizontal flip
journey.result: Original 13 photos: precision 73.5%, recall 75.6%, mAP@50 0.846. New 31-photo test: 64.7% / 64.9% / 0.675
journey.lesson: Bigger input and honest evaluation. Recall on the original photos rose 26 points.

journey.done: Experiment: synthetic dashboards with small glowing icons
journey.result: No measurable gain (fine-tune control mAP@50 0.690 / 0.611 vs 0.641 / 0.586 with synthetic data, validation / test)
journey.lesson: Dropped. A tested idea that did not work.

journey.done: Reviewed 259 model-vs-label disagreements and 75 missed objects
journey.result: 12 corrections: 6 wrong classes, 2 missing labels, 4 duplicated boxes
journey.lesson: Far fewer label errors than expected; most "false" detections were look-alike variants the dataset leaves unlabelled on purpose.

journey.done: Replaced Roboflow's pre-rotated, mirrored, blurred copies with un-augmented originals
journey.result: R2 re-scored on clean, corrected photos: validation 73.9% / 76.2% / 0.840, test 69.6% / 67.5% / 0.774
journey.lesson: Part of the earlier gap was the evaluation images, not the model.

journey.done: Fine-tuned R2 on clean originals + corrected labels + 458 hard negatives (close-ups of door-open, lane-departure, washer-fluid, power-steering, seat-belt, low-fuel symbols)
journey.result: Test at confidence 0.40: precision 81.4% -> 85.3%, recall 64.0% -> 71.9%. Test mAP@50 0.774 -> 0.821
journey.lesson: Negatives raised precision; recall on small lights improved from 64% to 72%.

limitations: The evaluation set is small: 49 photos and 145 lights. A few objects move a percentage by several points.
ESP (7 evaluation objects) and master warning (2) are barely tested.
Small lights are the weak spot: 72% found below 24 px.
Large close-up icons got slightly worse in R4 (3 of 9 found, was 5 of 9).
The dataset does not label look-alike variants (ESP OFF, the yellow "(!)" light, the "(P)" parking-brake light), so the model is trained to ignore them.
Evaluation photos are web and stock images resized to 640 px; performance on phone photos of a real dashboard is not measured.
The model identifies symbols. It does not diagnose a vehicle.
